$comment: the openapi family specifications section 9.2 normalized-collision CONFINEMENT, shared byte-identically by the two client engines and the two adapter engines. Two keys in ONE content map denoting the same parsed media type are a normalized collision, and the defect confines to that colliding parsed identity -- the smallest unit that owns it. No first-key rule: no request selection may land on the colliding identity and no response match may be governed by it, each such selection refusing with the exclusion accounted, while the map's non-colliding entries remain usable alternatives. 'side' names which content map the cell exercises. Request cells carry the synthesis coverage accounting the adapters emit ('target', 'represented', 'excluded', 'collidingIdentity'); response cells carry the advertised success-media membership ('advertised'), which is the Accept set the clients emit.

cases.name: request-collision-confines-and-the-sibling-selects
cases.description: Two spellings of application/json collide in one content map; the non-colliding sibling is still a usable alternative and dispatches under its own declaration.

cases.name: request-selection-may-not-land-on-the-colliding-identity
cases.description: The same map, selecting the colliding identity itself: no request selection may land on it, so the invocation refuses before dispatch even though a usable sibling exists.

cases.name: request-map-whose-only-entries-collide-refuses
cases.description: A map with no non-colliding entry left has no candidate carriage at all: the required body refuses and the target is accounted excluded.

cases.name: request-control-no-collision
cases.description: Control: two distinct parsed identities in one map collide with nothing, so both stay represented and the selection dispatches.

cases.name: request-collision-confines-on-the-3.0-line
cases.description: The rule is edition-uniform: a bare type/subtype case collision on the 3.0 line confines exactly as a parameterized one does on the 3.1 line.

cases.name: response-collision-confines-and-the-sibling-governs
cases.description: A collision in a response content map does not poison a clean concrete match: the non-colliding text/plain sibling still governs the decode, and only it is advertised.

cases.name: response-match-may-not-be-governed-by-the-colliding-identity
cases.description: The same map, with the peer selecting the colliding identity: no response match may be governed by it, so the interaction fails loudly rather than picking a key by source order.

cases.name: response-range-collision-confines-to-the-range-identity
cases.description: Two colliding RANGE keys own only their own range identity: a clean concrete application/json declaration still governs the decode.

cases.name: response-map-whose-only-entries-collide-governs-nothing
cases.description: A response map with no non-colliding entry left governs nothing, and advertises nothing: the Accept set is empty rather than naming a representation the decode lane must refuse.

cases.name: response-control-no-collision
cases.description: Control: two distinct parsed identities govern and advertise normally.

cases.name: response-collision-confines-on-the-3.0-line
cases.description: The response half is edition-uniform too: a bare case collision on the 3.0 line confines to its identity and leaves the sibling governing.
